title: Priming-aware staged data-plane rollout and rollback operator
creator: Daniel Kim
description:
Problem: Private (VPC) data-plane/runtime upgrades can cause transient application errors and throughput regression if KV caches, session state, or in-flight streams are not primed before traffic is shifted. Our current operator performs blue/green swaps but lacks a deterministic priming phase and multi-signal health acceptance which leads to noisy rollouts and manual rollbacks.

Goal: Implement an operator-driven staged rollout that: (1) creates a primed candidate set of nodes with warmed KV caches and model KV caches via traffic-shadowing and synthetic priming; (2) advances traffic in small increments using canary percentages and multi-signal health checks; (3) supports fast automated rollback based on defined criteria; and (4) exposes Terraform/IaC hooks so customers on Redwood Private can opt in to safe upgrades with zero-downtime guarantees in their VPCs.

Constraints: Must work offline in air-gapped deployments, respect customer network egress policies, play well with Dedicated vs Private resource sizing, and not require model re-serialization. Non-goal: Rewriting the runtime; this is orchestration and operator-layer automation only.
acceptance_criteria: Operator can create a candidate data-plane pool and perform synthetic KV/model cache priming before any production traffic is shifted.
Traffic can be progressively shifted 0% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with adjustable hold windows and automated health checks between steps.
Health evaluation must consider at least 3 signals: per-route latency P95, token error-rate, and end-to-end success rate from a customer-like synthetic workload.
Automated rollback triggers when any health signal breaches configured thresholds for a configurable consecutive-window (default 3 checks).
Terraform module exposes a boolean flag (safe_rollout_enabled) and parameters for canary schedule, priming-samples, and rollback thresholds; tests and docs included.
Runbook commands are available to forcibly abort, promote, or rollback a rollout with expected state and telemetry checks documented.
E2E test in our staging cluster demonstrates no request failures for a representative RLHF-style chat workload during a full rollout with priming enabled.
implementation_notes: Extend upgrade operator to create a 'priming' phase: spin up candidate VMs/containers with identical model/weights and warm KV caches by replaying recent request prefixes and targeted synthetic sequences.
Add traffic-shadowing (mirror) support in the kube ingress/agent to direct a configurable fraction of live requests to candidates for priming without affecting production metrics.
Implement a multi-signal aggregator in the operator that ingests metrics from Console metrics API and our runtime health endpoints; expose pluggable thresholds via CRD and Terraform variables.
Tie into Terraform via new modules/private_rollout.tf that annotate the operator CR with module-managed rollout policies; ensure state is idempotent and safe to reapply.
Cache priming should be rate-limited and TTL aware: don't exceed normal token-per-second budgets and avoid evicting live caches on host by prioritizing candidate warming frequency.
Instrument rollout with tracing labels and add per-candidate trace sampling to locate regressions tied to kernel selection or quantization paths.
Provide a dry-run mode that exercises priming and health checks without touching traffic routing to validate in customer environments.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Prepare: validate operator has required IAM and KMS access, Terraform apply creates candidate pool but does not modify service routing.

Phase 1 - Priming (0-30m): traffic-shadow 5% of requests and run synthetic request set (configurable default: 2000 unique prefixes) targeting model KV and prefix caches; success criteria: 95% of synthetic requests return <1s per-token latency on candidate nodes.
Phase 2 - Canary (1% traffic, hold 10m): route 1% to candidate; run multi-signal check (latency P95, error rate <0.1%, success rate >99%).
Phase 3 - Ramp (5% -> 20% -> 50%): increment holds of 10m/15m/20m respectively; if any check fails, operator pauses and starts rollback timer.
Phase 4 - Promote (100%): final switch after 50% stable for 20m; operator finalizes decommission of old nodes with graceful drain for 10m.
Operator provides a 'fast rollback' path: immediate route revert and tombstone candidate nodes, followed by postmortem instrumentation capture.
rollback_criteria: Latency: per-route P95 increases by >30% relative to baseline for 3 consecutive checks
Errors: tokenization/decoding errors or 5xx downstream errors exceed 0.2% of requests over a 5m window
Quality regression: automated evals on a small held-out prompt set drop in pass@k or confidence metrics beyond configured threshold
Resource pressure: GPU memory OOMs, sustained swap usage, or node-level kernel faults observed by runtime probes
Manual abort: on-call or SRE can initiate rollback via operator CLI or Console action with a single confirm step.
runbook_snippet:
To abort rollout:
  1) rctl operator abort-rollout --id <rollout-id>
  2) terraform apply -var 'safe_rollout_enabled=false' to ensure no automated retries
  3) verify old-pool nodes health: curl https://console/api/internal/health or use dashboard 'Private Runtime' > 'Active Pools'
To force promote after manual validation: rctl operator promote-rollout --id <rollout-id> --force
notes: 03/14 - PM review (María López): requested explicit Terraform knobs for priming-samples and traffic-mirror-rate; added to implementation notes.
03/18 - Security review kickoff: operator will need KMS decrypt to read model keys in candidate pods; SRE to verify key rotation compatibility.
03/20 - Design review (Ethan Zhao): recommended adding a synthetic 'cold-start' workload to simulate first-time KV misses during priming; accepted.
03/22 - SRE feedback (Anna Müller): suggest extending drain timeout for sessions with long-lived streaming to 15m for chat customers; updated rollout plan.
03/24 - QA: creating e2e test harness that replays production traces to ensure priming does not regress throughput under burst scenarios.
